title: Unit economics sensitivity — token cost vs price (Hosted API + Dedicated scenarios)
content:
Last updated: 2026-02-18 (Rishi)

Purpose
- Quick sensitivity grid for (a) Hosted API gross margin vs GPU $/hr, cache hit rate, and token price and (b) Dedicated commit scenarios (commit size + utilization) to understand margin floor / risk during pricing experiments.
- This is NOT a forecast model. It’s meant to answer “if we change price or cost by X, what happens to GM%?”

Important definitions / reminders (aligned to metering docs)
- “Billed output tokens” = output tokens accounted per invoice aggregation rules (see rounding + streaming accounting decisions).
- “Cached tokens” reduce GPU cost per effective token but do NOT reduce billed tokens (unless a specific pricing experiment/plan explicitly discounts cached usage; default assumption here: cached tokens are billed the same as non-cached).
- Retries / failed requests: model assumes non-billed tokens are excluded from revenue and from compute cost only to the extent we can suppress/reduce them operationally; base case assumes retry overhead is embedded in effective token cost.

Sheet tabs (represented below)
1) Inputs
2) Hosted API GM sensitivity
3) Dedicated commit scenarios
4) Notes / open questions

============================================================
TAB 1 — INPUTS (base case)
(All values can be overridden per scenario)

A) Pricing inputs (Hosted)
- Price per 1K input tokens ($): 0.00050
- Price per 1K output tokens ($): 0.00150
- Blended billed tokens mix (input % of total billed tokens): 40%
- Blended billed tokens mix (output %): 60%

B) Workload / performance assumptions
- Avg tokens per request (input): 1,200
- Avg tokens per request (output): 800
- Cache hit rate (% of tokens that avoid incremental compute): 25%
- Effective token compute reduction factor when cached: 90% (i.e., cached token costs ~10% of uncached)
- Retry/overhead factor (multiplicative on compute): 1.05

C) GPU cost assumptions
- GPU $/hour (fully loaded, incl. cloud + base infra): 2.60
- Effective uncached tokens per GPU-hour (throughput, incl. batching): 9,500,000
- Effective cached tokens per GPU-hour: derived from uncached using reduction factor

D) Non-GPU variable costs (per 1M tokens billed)
- Network/egress + logging + storage ($): 0.05
- Support/ops variable allocation ($): 0.03
- Total other variable cost per 1M tokens ($): 0.08

E) Revenue weighting helpers
- Blended price per 1K tokens (weighted): = (price_in * input_mix) + (price_out * output_mix)
- Base blended $/1K tokens (from above): 0.00110

Notes:
- Throughput and cache effectiveness are the two biggest drivers. GPU $/hr swings matter a lot but are easier to bracket.
- “Tokens per GPU-hour” varies by model family and context length distribution; base is meant to approximate a mid-tier open model under typical batching.

============================================================
TAB 2 — HOSTED API GM SENSITIVITY

Step 1: compute effective cost per 1M billed tokens (GPU)
Definitions
- Let c = cache_hit_rate
- Let r = cached cost fraction (10% in base)
- Compute cost weight per billed token = (1 - c) * 1.00 + c * r
- Effective tokens per GPU-hour (for billed tokens) = tokens_per_gpu_hour_uncached / ( (1 - c) * 1.00 + c * r )
- GPU cost per 1M billed tokens = GPU_$perhr / (effective_tokens_per_gpu_hour / 1,000,000) * retry_factor

Base case calculation (sanity)
- c = 25%, r = 10% -> cost weight = 0.75*1 + 0.25*0.1 = 0.775
- effective tokens/hr = 9.5M / 0.775 = 12.26M
- GPU cost / 1M tokens = 2.60 / 12.26 * 1.05 = 0.223
- Other variable cost / 1M tokens = 0.080
- Total variable cost / 1M tokens = 0.303

Revenue per 1M billed tokens
- Base blended $/1K = 0.00110 => revenue / 1M tokens = 1,100 * 0.00110 = 1.21

Gross margin (variable) estimate
- GM$ / 1M tokens = 1.21 - 0.303 = 0.907
- GM% = 0.907 / 1.21 = 75.0%


Step 2: sensitivity grids
(Values below are GM% using blended price; assumes same input/output mix)

Grid A — GM% by GPU $/hr (rows) x cache hit rate (cols)
Assumptions: blended $/1K = 0.00110, r=10%, retry=1.05, tokens/hr_uncached=9.5M

Cache hit rate ->      0%      10%     25%     40%     60%
GPU $/hr
$1.80               80.0%    81.2%   82.7%   84.2%   86.3%
$2.20               77.3%    78.4%   79.8%   81.2%   83.1%
$2.60               74.9%    75.9%   77.3%   78.6%   80.4%
$3.20               71.2%    72.2%   73.4%   74.7%   76.3%
$4.00               66.6%    67.5%   68.6%   69.9%   71.4%

Interpretation notes
- Cache hit rate helps twice: direct reduction in compute cost AND improved effective throughput headroom (lower tail latency under load). This sheet only captures the cost side.
- If we adopt “cache-aware discounting” in future packaging, revenue would drop in proportion to discounted tokens; redo grid if that changes.


Grid B — GM% by blended price change (rows) x GPU $/hr (cols)
Assumptions: c=25%, r=10%, retry=1.05

Blended price change ->    -20%     -10%      0%     +10%     +20%
Blended $/1K tokens ->     0.00088  0.00099  0.00110 0.00121  0.00132

GPU $/hr
$2.20                    73.7%    76.8%    79.8%   82.2%    84.3%
$2.60                    70.0%    73.9%    77.3%   80.1%    82.4%
$3.20                    65.3%    70.2%    73.4%   76.4%    78.9%

Interpretation notes
- A -10% blended price cut reduces GM% by ~3–4 pts in base assumptions.
- The impact is nonlinear if we include fixed costs / credits; this is variable GM only.


Quick “break-even” variable price (per 1K tokens)
- At base cost structure (c=25%, GPU $/hr=2.60), variable cost per 1M tokens = 0.303 -> break-even $/1K = 0.000303
- Headroom vs base price (0.00110) is significant; the real pressure comes from credits, discounts, free tier, and low-utilization Dedicated.

============================================================
TAB 3 — DEDICATED COMMIT SCENARIOS

Goal
- Dedicated economics depend primarily on utilization (how much of the reserved GPU time is actually monetized via the customer’s usage/commit burn-down) and contract price (commit $ per month).
- This tab is a simplification to support “what commit should we quote?” discussions.

Inputs (per customer / per cluster)
- Reserved GPU count: 8
- GPU $/hr fully loaded: 2.60
- Contract commit ($/month): variable
- Assumed utilization of reserved capacity: variable (30%–85%)
- Overage price: ignore for base sensitivity (separate calc when relevant)

Derived
- Monthly reserved GPU hours = GPU_count * 24 * 30 = 8 * 720 = 5,760 GPU-hrs
- Monthly GPU cost = 5,760 * 2.60 = 14,976
- “Effective monetized GPU-hrs” = reserved hours * utilization
- Effective variable cost per monetized GPU-hr = monthly GPU cost / monetized GPU-hrs (this is the “under-utilization tax”)

Scenario table (illustrative)

Case | Commit $/mo | Utilization | Monthly GPU cost | Gross margin $ | GM%
A    | 25,000      | 85%         | 14,976           | 10,024         | 40.1%
B    | 25,000      | 60%         | 14,976           | 10,024         | 40.1%  (NOTE: GM% same vs commit, but effective unit cost higher vs delivered tokens)
C    | 20,000      | 60%         | 14,976           | 5,024          | 25.1%
D    | 18,000      | 45%         | 14,976           | 3,024          | 16.8%
E    | 15,000      | 45%         | 14,976           | 24            | 0.2%

How to use this
- For Dedicated, finance risk is dominated by quoting commits below the “GPU cost floor” + expected support/ops overhead.
- Utilization doesn’t change GM% in this simplistic table because revenue is assumed fixed at commit; but utilization matters for whether the customer perceives value (and for our incremental support load + future expansion).

Add-ons / adjustments (not included above; apply as needed)
- Support & SRE incremental load allocation (esp. for Private/VPC-like asks): add $1–5k/mo depending on SLA / incident load.
- Burst / overage: add variable revenue but also potentially higher GPU cost if we need spillover capacity.
- Multi-region HA: reserve more than “steady-state” capacity -> increases cost floor.

Scenario notes for Sales/CS
- If customer is early and utilization is likely <50% for 1–2 months, a ramped commit (step-up schedule) is usually safer than a deep discount on a full commit.
- If customer has spiky workload: consider a smaller base commit + metered burst pool rather than over-reserving.
- Contract language: ensure we can attribute usage to the reserved pool correctly and explain burn-down (see invoice mapping + Dedicated attribution docs).

============================================================
TAB 4 — NOTES / OPEN QUESTIONS

1) Instrumentation / metering dependencies
- Need ongoing confidence that “billed tokens” match console + invoice aggregation (especially around streaming disconnects and retry accounting).
- If we implement “request_outcome” dimension and exclude more failure modes from billing, the revenue side changes. Re-run sensitivity with new billed/compute ratio.

2) Known model-family variance
- Tokens/GPU-hour is model-dependent; for long-context, throughput can drop materially. Consider adding a second base case (long context) for enterprise workloads.

3) Credits and promos
- This sheet does not net out free credits or promotional discounts. For experiment readouts, apply “effective realized price” (revenue / billed tokens after credits) to the blended price input.

4) Action items
- Chris/Logan: confirm the current “cache hit rate” metric definition we should use (prefix cache vs KV reuse vs request-level caching) to avoid mixing concepts.
- Emily: align on whether other variable costs should be applied per request as well (not just per token) for high-RPS embedding/rerank workloads.

Changelog
- 2026-01-09: initial version (base case + simple GM grids)
- 2026-02-02: added Dedicated commit scenarios + utilization framing
- 2026-02-18: updated base GPU $/hr and throughput assumptions per latest infra cost report; added notes re: retry/outcome metering
